tracks.name: IT Infrastructure & Support
tracks.role_in_simulation: Central nervous system — manages identities, licenses, and the internal helpdesk for the entire cohort. Every other track depends on this one for access.

tools.name: Google Workspace Business Starter
tools.why_chosen: Simpler admin panel, better real-time collaboration, and 90% of Berlin startups run on it.

tools.name: Google Admin Console
tools.why_chosen: One-click offboarding, group-based access, OAuth app management. No separate Entra ID bill.

tools.name: Jira Cloud
tools.why_chosen: Purpose-built for agile teams. Confluence integrates natively. ServiceNow's ITIL rigidity kills startup velocity.

tools.name: 1Password Teams
tools.why_chosen: Replaces AD password complexity. Participants learn secrets management, which is more relevant than Group Policy.

tools.name: Slack
tools.why_chosen: Every Berlin startup uses it. Participants learn Slack threading and channel hygiene.

tracks.name: Data Analytics & Engineering
tracks.role_in_simulation: Decision-support engine — builds the shared data warehouse and dashboards that Marketing and IT consume. Maintains the single source of truth for the simulated company.

tools.name: PostgreSQL 16
tools.why_chosen: The standard for startup data stacks. Teaches the SQL dialect students will actually use.

tools.name: DuckDB
tools.why_chosen: The biggest shift in analytics since Spark. Runs analytical queries on CSV/Parquet locally with zero infrastructure. Perfect for teaching ETL without cloud bills.

tools.name: dbt Core (CLI)
tools.why_chosen: Same SQL-based transformation logic as dbt Cloud, but runs in GitHub Actions or locally. Students learn the actual tool, not a SaaS wrapper.

tools.name: MotherDuck
tools.why_chosen: If you need a shared cloud warehouse, MotherDuck is DuckDB-as-a-service. Way cheaper than Snowflake/BigQuery for small data.

tools.name: Metabase (self-hosted)
tools.why_chosen: The startup standard. Ask questions in SQL or GUI, build dashboards, embed sharing. Replaces Tableau/Power BI at 1/10th the cost.

tools.name: GitHub Actions
tools.why_chosen: Replaces expensive orchestrators (Airflow Cloud). Students learn Git + automation together.

tools.name: Railway / DigitalOcean
tools.why_chosen: Simple, predictable pricing. No surprise compute bills.

tracks.name: Digital Marketing & Content
tracks.role_in_simulation: Growth & visibility arm — drives simulated lead generation and brand awareness. Depends on the Data track for performance dashboards and on the IT track for tool access and domain management.

tools.name: Webflow (Basic)
tools.why_chosen: Visual builder, built-in hosting, SEO controls, and CMS collections. Marketers can build landing pages without touching PHP or plugins. The modern startup standard over WordPress.

tools.name: Ghost (Starter)
tools.why_chosen: If the cohort focuses on content marketing and newsletters, Ghost is superior to WordPress. Clean editor, native newsletter delivery, no plugin hell.

tools.name: Canva
tools.free_tier_limit: Full free tier sufficient for simulation
tools.why_chosen: Marketers need rapid asset creation. The free tier is sufficient for a simulation.

tools.name: Figma
tools.why_chosen: Clarify the boundary: Canva = marketing assets; Figma = web/UI layout. If budget is tight, marketers can prototype in Figma and export assets.

tools.name: Notion
tools.why_chosen: Marketing teams run their entire editorial calendar in Notion. Replaces scattered WordPress admin notes.

tools.name: Beehiiv
tools.why_chosen: Better analytics than Mailchimp and built for growth. Perfect for simulating a SaaS newsletter.

tools.name: Google Analytics 4
tools.why_chosen: Industry standard. Free and comprehensive.

tools.name: Google Search Console
tools.why_chosen: Essential for teaching technical SEO basics.
